samples.summary: Enforce-by-default fires before the documented "does a viewer emit verb rw?" question is answered — a stock deployment that registers the webhook methods may deny every viewer-role share-link attach/sync
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` returns true for anything but the literal `false`, so registering the methods and configuring nothing else now enforces. But `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:254-267` records the verb question as OPEN: Yorkie derives the verb from the change pack (`AccessAttributes(pack)` → `rw` when `pack.HasChanges()`), "the React `DocumentProvider` does not currently expose a read-only/`syncMode` attach option, so this can't be forced from the frontend today", and the stated mitigation is "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping". A viewer share mount still attaches with `initialPresence` (`shared-document.tsx:993-999`), and a presence change is a change in the attach pack — which would make the verb `rw`, and `hasAccess` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:269) refuses `rw` for `link.role !== 'editor'`. Under the old shadow default that produced a log line; under the new default it produces a 403 that breaks read-only share links (notes, docs, slides, board) on the very first attach. The change removes the observation step that was the mitigation without resolving the risk it mitigated.
searchedFor: shared-document.tsx DocumentProvider initialRoot/initialPresence for each type

samples.summary: Share-link image upload failures are silent: `shareTokenImageUploader` rejects, but the notes engine's `UploadImage` contract expects the host to resolve `null` after reporting the error itself
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` is a `DocsImageUpload` that throws on any failure (image-insert.ts:40-49 — `postShareTokenImage` rejects). The notes engine documents the other contract: `UploadImage` resolving `null` means "the host handled the failure itself", and a rejected promise is merely logged (`image-upload.ts:179-190` → `console.error('Image upload failed', err)`), placeholder dropped, no user-visible feedback. The workspace route wraps its uploader in try/catch + `toast.error` (notes-detail.tsx:208-231) and the docs share path goes through `insertImageFromFile`, which toasts (image-insert.ts:144-151). So an editor-role visitor whose upload fails (413, network, unsupported type, revoked link) sees the ghost vanish with no explanation.

samples.summary: Divider drag: `track` can be zero or negative (division by zero → NaN/Infinity flex basis), and the ratio places the divider's LEFT EDGE at the pointer, so the 25px band now sits ~12px right of the finger
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` then `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;`. With a container no wider than the divider (25px) `track` is 0 → `ratio` is ±Infinity or NaN (jsdom/zero-width measurement gives `0/0` = NaN, which flows into `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` = NaN and then into `flex: 1 1 NaN%`); negative `track` inverts the drag direction. Separately, a pane's final width is exactly `ratio * track`, so setting `ratio = (x - left)/track` puts the divider's left edge under the pointer rather than its centre — a half-width (12.5px) lag that the comment claims to have fixed but only reduced.

samples.summary: New comments in this same change assert the opposite of the new default ("the webhook allows everything until … `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`" / "ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default")
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:63-64` (added by this change) says the webhook "allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`", and `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:446-448` (also added here) says it "ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default" — both contradict `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (enforce unless the literal `false`). The same stale claim survives in `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40`, `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413`, `docs/design/sharing.md:208`, `docs/design/template-gallery.md:668` and `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301`. A future reader deciding whether a client-side guard is load-bearing will read the wrong deployment posture. Also note `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185` says only the exact value `false` opts out, while the helper accepts `FALSE` and `' false '`.

samples.summary: `YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor subscription is never unsubscribed, so every NotesView remount leaks a document listener (path this change re-touches when it wraps the store)
samples.evidence: The constructor calls `doc.subscribe(...)` (line 143) to capture undo/redo selections and discards the returned unsubscribe; `NoteStore` exposes no dispose, and `notes-view.tsx`'s cleanup only calls `editor.dispose()` and clears the refs (lines 167-172). A new `YorkieNoteStore` is built on every effect run — e.g. `key={historyResetToken}` remounts after a revision restore (notes-detail.tsx:320) and dev HMR — so each remount adds a permanent listener holding the dead store. The read-only wrapper does not change this (it forwards nothing that could dispose it) and hides no field, so nothing external can clean it up either.

samples.summary: `canUndo`/`canRedo` are forwarded to the real store while `undo`/`redo` are neutered, so the guarded handle reports "there is something to undo" and then does nothing
samples.evidence: `NOTE_STORE_READERS` includes `canUndo`/`canRedo` (bound to the target), while `HISTORY_METHODS` makes `undo`/`redo` return `null`. Any holder of the wrapped store other than `initialize` (which masks it with `!readOnly && store.canUndo()`, editor.ts:674-675) sees an inconsistent contract: the interface documents `undo()` as a no-op returning `null` only "when `canUndo()` is false".

verdict.reason: Every element the reviewer cites is present verbatim. `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22) enforces for anything but the literal 'false', so registering the webhook methods and configuring nothing else enforces immediately (self-hosting.md:584-587). Under enforcement, a share-link viewer's attribute with verb 'rw' is refused: checkAttribute sets needWrite from `attr.verb === 'rw'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:233) and hasAccess returns `link.role === 'editor'` for share identities (line 269), with the response status set to 403 (lines 173-174). There is no exemption for AttachDocument — only DetachDocument (line 54) and the two client methods (line 57) bypass the check — so no guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. The verb risk is recorded as UNRESOLVED in the repo's own design doc (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:254-267): Yorkie derives the verb from the change pack, the React DocumentProvider exposes no read-only/syncMode attach option, and the stated mitigation is to observe shadow logs before flipping. Every viewer share mount still attaches with initialPresence (shared-document.tsx:975, 984, 993-999, 1008, 1021), and a presence set is a local change in the attach pack. I confirmed no frontend read-only attach path exists — the only `syncMode: 'readonly'` usages are backend server-side attaches (docs-content.controller.ts:130). I cannot prove from this repository whether Yorkie's Pack.HasChanges() counts a presence-only change, and that unresolvable uncertainty is exactly what the removed observation step was for; a 403 on the first viewer attach would break read-only share links for notes/docs/slides/board, which is a core-flow break under the correctness rubric. No named refutation ground applies.
